insurer: Aditya Birla Health Insurance Co. Limited
sumInsured: ₹50 Lakhs to ₹6 Crores (as per Product Benefit Table)

great.name: Room rent: No limit (At actuals up to Sum Insured)
great.quote: Room Rent ... Actuals up to Sum Insured
great.reference: Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (VIP+), Hospitalization Treatment (In-built Cover)
great.explanation: No room category restriction/cap in the benefit table, so you can choose any room and the eligible room rent is covered up to your Sum Insured (subject to overall policy terms).

great.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: 90 days
great.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred... for up to 90 days immediately prior to the date of such Hospitalization.
great.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for the same condition for up to 90 days before admission (better than standard 30–60 days).

great.name: Built-in restore/reload benefit: Super Reload (unlimited refills; from 2nd claim of policy life as per PBT)
great.quote: We shall provide for a reload amounting to the Base Sum Insured (“Super Reload”), unlimited times during the Policy Year...
great.explanation: Once your Base SI + Super Credit (if applicable) is exhausted/insufficient, the policy can reload SI multiple times in a year (conditions apply; the product benefit table notes availability from the 2nd claim of policy life).

great.name: Built-in additional Sum Insured buffer: Super Credit (added irrespective of claims)
great.quote: an additional limit under the current Policy Year (“Super Credit”) will be applied / increased... irrespective of any claims in previous Policy Year
great.explanation: This is extra coverage over and above Base SI that accrues on renewal even if you made a claim (a strong feature because it does not depend on being claim-free).

great.name: NCB / Renewal bonus: Non-resetting renewal addition (Super Credit)
great.explanation: Renewal bonus does not reset to zero due to claims, because it is explicitly stated to increase irrespective of claim.

great.name: Consumables / non-medical expenses: Covered if Claim Protect is in force (all 4 lists)
great.quote: Claim Protect (Non-Medical Expense Waiver): Non-payable items will be covered (all 4 lists of Annexure I)
great.reference: Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (VIP+); also Section C.4
great.explanation: If Claim Protect is applicable to you (in force as per your Policy Schedule), common non-medical hospital bill items (gloves, masks, etc. per Annexure I lists) are covered instead of being out-of-pocket.

great.name: Bariatric/obesity surgery: Covered (subject to conditions)
great.quote: Obesity Treatment: Medical Expenses incurred... for a Bariatric Surgery... subject to the conditions that needs to be fulfilled as per Section D.1.6
great.explanation: Bariatric surgery is covered when the policy’s medical criteria are met.

good.name: Specific illness/procedure waiting period: 24 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries / treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...
good.reference: Section D.1.2 Specified disease / procedure Waiting Period (Code-Excl02)
good.explanation: A 24-month specific illness waiting period is standard in the market.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days (except accident)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: 30 days is standard for new policies (accidents are typically exempt).

good.name: PED waiting period: 3 years
good.quote:
Pre Existing Disease (PED) Waiting Period
3 years
good.reference: Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (VIP+), Waiting Period - Inbuilt Cover
good.explanation: A 3-year PED waiting period is within the acceptable standard range (2–4 years).

bad.name: Post-hospitalization cover limited to 180 days (not >180 days)
bad.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred... for up to 180 days from the date of discharge from the Hospital.
bad.explanation: 180 days is good/standard, but not best-in-class (>180 days). If you need longer follow-up care, expenses after 180 days may be out-of-pocket.

bad.name: Consumables not covered by default (Claim Protect required)
bad.quote: The expenses that are not covered... may be covered under this Product if Claim Protect (Non-Medical Expense Waiver) is applicable to You and mentioned in the Policy Schedule.
bad.reference: Annexure Summary; also Section C.4 / Annexure I context
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items are not automatically covered for everyone; they are covered only if Claim Protect is applicable and shown as in-force in your Policy Schedule.

unclear.name: Co-pay (copayment) terms
unclear.quote: Co-Payment: means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the Policyholder / Insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
unclear.explanation: The wording defines what co-pay is, but does not clearly state whether any co-pay applies by default for this plan/variant and for which ages/claims. Verify co-pay (if any) from the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table for your issued policy.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
